title: Plant Nuclear Genomic DNA Preparations
author: Elena Hilario

materials: Adjust the volume to 294 mL with NEB complete buffer

If the interphase between the organic and aqueous solutions is not tight, you could centrigue the sample for another 15 min or transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube and add equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol go to step #34 go to step #35

Follow the Qiagen DNease Plant Maxi kit instructions with the following modifications: The final pellet of nuclei should be divided into 2 tubes and treat each one as the starting material for one extraction using this kit To elute the DNA incubate the binding column with 1 mL of AE buffer for 1 h. Spin down as described in the kit instructions. Add another mL of AE buffer to the binding column and incubate at room temperature for 30 min. Spin down again. Each column/tube will have ~ 2 mL of eluted DNA Combine both samples (~ 4 mL) and add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2, mix, and add 2 volumes of 100% ethanol. Mix. Store at 4°C or -20°C ovenight Collect, wash and resuspend the pellet as described in steps 26-30 The fragment size distribution obtained with this kit is 20-40 kbp

steps.title: Homogenize Plant Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize kiwifruit leaves in ice-cold buffer using a blender inside a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Pour 300 mL ice-cold NEB complete buffer into a blender.
Weight 20 g of kiwifruit leaves, cut any long stems, and transfer to the blender.
Homogenize for 30 sec on low setting (or High if using a kitchen blender); do not use a stick hand-held blender.

steps.title: Filter Homogenate
steps.instruction: Perform a two-stage filtration of the homogenate using cheesecloth and miracloth.

substeps.instruction: Filtrate homogenate through 4 layers of cheesecloth (or disposable kitchen cloth like CHUX superwipes) into a sterile glass cylinder.
Filter the resulting liquid again through 4 layers of miracloth (stacked perpendicular to the fabric grain) into another 500 mL sterile glass cylinder.

steps.title: Permeabilize Nuclei
steps.instruction: Add Triton X-100 to the homogenate to permeabilize the sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 6 mL of 25% Triton X-100 in NEB complete buffer by placing the pipette tip on the inside wall of the cylinder near the top, dispensing slowly while rotating the cylinder.
Seal the cylinder with parafilm and mix very gently by inversion 10-20 times, rotating the cylinder during each mix.

steps.title: Remove Cellular Debris
steps.instruction: Perform a low-speed centrifugation to remove large debris.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot the homogenate into six 50 mL Falcon tubes (or Nalgene centrifuge tubes).
Spin down at 588 rpm (57 g) using the SLA-600 TC rotor (or equivalent g-force for SS34 rotor) at 4-10°C for 2 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a new set of 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Spin down at 3308 rpm (1800 g) using the SLA-600 TC rotor at 10°C for 15 min.

steps.title: Wash Nuclei Pellets
steps.instruction: Wash the nuclei pellets to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant into a waste container (following b-mercaptoethanol regulations).
Resuspend each pellet with 50 mL NEB buffer (without β-mercaptoethanol), mix gently by inversion, and spin down again as in the previous step.
Discard the supernatant (this can be poured down the drain if not regulated biological material).

steps.title: Collect and Quantify Nuclei
steps.instruction: Pool the washed nuclei and determine the total mass.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet with 5 mL NEB buffer (without β-mercaptoethanol).
Collect all pellets into one previously weighted Falcon tube.
Add more NEB buffer (without β-mercaptoethanol) to reach a final volume of 50 mL.
Weight the tube to determine the total amount of isolated nuclei (expected ~0.2 g from 20 g leaves).
Keep the tube on ice or store the pellet at -80°C.

steps.title: Lysis and RNA Digestion
steps.instruction: Lyse the nuclei and remove RNA using RNase A.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend 0.2 g of nuclei pellet in 14 mL lysis buffer; mix by inversion (do not vortex).
Add 7 μL of RNase A (100 mg/mL) and mix by inversion.
Incubate for 10 min at 37°C with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Precipitate the genomic DNA using K-Acetate and Ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.4 mL 5 M K-Acetate (pH 7) and mix by inversion.
Add 3.5 mL 100% Ethanol and vortex at maximum speed for 30 s.

steps.title: Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Purify the DNA by removing proteins and lipids with chloroform:isoamyl alcohol.

substeps.instruction: Extract the sample with an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1).
Mix by inversion 10 times, then shake horizontally in an orbital shaker at room temperature for 5 min.
Spin down at 3000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature using a swing bucket rotor.

steps.title: Isopropanol Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA from the aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase to a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add an equal volume of ice-cold isopropanol, mix by inversion, and store at -20°C for 30 min.
Spin down at 3000 rpm for 25 min at room temperature or 10°C.

steps.title: Wash and Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Clean the DNA pellet and resuspend in TE buffer.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and remove ethanol traces with a kimwipe.
Air dry the pellet at room temperature for 20-30 min.
Discard supernatant and add the same volume of 70% ethanol to wash the pellet; let stand for ~10 min.
Collect DNA by centrifugation.
Add 100-200 μL TE buffer (pH 7.5). Tap the bottom of the tube to detach the pellet.
Allow the DNA to diffuse slowly at room temperature for a few hours or in the refrigerator overnight (avoid high-speed vortexing).
Store at 4°C for short term.
For long term, make numbered aliquots and store at -20°C, avoiding freeze/thaw cycles.

steps.title: Alternative CTAB Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform an alternative extraction using CTAB/NaCl if required.

substeps.instruction: Add 3.5 mL CTAB/NaCl extraction buffer and 80 μL Proteinase K to the nuclei pellet and vortex gently to resuspend.
Incubate at 56°C for 1-2 hours without shaking until the solution is clear.
Add 3.5 mL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1) and vortex until an emulsion is obtained.
Centrifuge using a swing bucket rotor at 3000 rpm at room temperature for 15 min.
Transfer the aqueous phase to a new Falcon tube, add 2 volumes of 100% ethanol, mix gently, and incubate at -20°C for at least 2 h.
Collect DNA by centrifugation, wash with 70% ethanol (as described in the previous method), and elute.

steps.title: Final DNA Treatment and QC
steps.instruction: Perform final RNA digestion and quality control checks.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 μL RNase A (100 mg/mL), mix, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Collect DNA by centrifugation.
Check quality via absorbance ratios (Aim for 260/280 ~1.8 and 260/230 >2.0).
Quantify ngDNA using fluorescence (Qubit or DeNovix) with a high sensitivity kit (10-fold serial dilutions, quantify 1-5 μL).
Run 100-200 ng of ngDNA on a 1% agarose gel stained with Sybr safe, using lambda DNA (48.5 kbp) as a control.
